en: The Vāsiṣṭhī Śikṣā, the Vāsiṣṭhī Śikṣā;
now I shall proclaim the Śikṣā according to the opinion of Vasiṣṭha.
Having extracted the entire sequence, the characteristic of the *Ṛg* and *Yajus* [portions] is as follows:
in the first chapter, in the ninth section (*anuvāka*), there is one verse beginning with "purākrūrasya";
all the mantras are *yajus*, numbering one hundred and seventeen *yajus* in the first [chapter].
In the second chapter: "vvītihotraṃ," "te 'gne," "marutāṃ pṛṣatīḥ," "yaṃ paridhiṃ"—these end with *yajus*;
"agneḥ priyaṃ yajuḥ," "saṃsravabhāgāḥ"—these end with *yajus*; "svāhā vāḍ" is one *yajus* together with a mantra; and "devā gātuvidaḥ" consists of two [mantras].
In the third chapter, there are two verses each for "saṃ vārccasi" and "ye rūpāṇyādhatte," making twelve verses; there are seventy-six *yajus* formulas;
and [the hymns] beginning with "samidhāgniṃ," "ā yad gaur," and "agnir jyotiḥ" consist of four, three, and [one verse] respectively.

The first seven are *gāyatrī* verses; five are within a single *ekapada*; "upaprayanta" is a *tripadā*; "ṣaḍindhānā" is a *tryavasānā*; and "mahāpaṅktirūpāśca" constitutes the seven *gāyatrīs*. There are three subsequent chapters consisting of *tripadās*, and four consisting of *dvipadās*: "somānam", "aganma", and "tisro gṛhā me".

"catasra upahūtāḥ" (four verses beginning with *catasra upahūtāḥ*) is a *mahāpaṅkti* with three pauses; "praghāsinaḥ" (four verses beginning with *praghāsinaḥ*); "pūrṇā darvī" (two verses beginning with *pūrṇā darvī*); "dve akṣann amīmadanta" (six verses beginning with *dve akṣann amīmadanta*); "eva rudram" (four verses beginning with *eva rudram*); and "etatte rudra" (one verse beginning with *etatte rudra*) is an *astārapaṅkti*. Some say this is the "recitation-sacrifice" (*japayajña*). "āyuṣam" (this verse) occurs in the third season. There are sixty-three or sixty-two *ṛc*s, and thirty-four or thirty-six *yajus* formulas in the fourth chapter. "edam" (two verses beginning with *edam*) are *atyaṣṭī*s with three pauses; "āvaḥ" (one verse beginning with *āvaḥ*); and "apo devīḥ" and "viśvo devasya".
"Daivīṃ dhiyam," "śvātrāḥ pītāḥ," "agne tvaṃ," "tvaṃ agne vvaravyasi," "samaravye abhityam," one each [of these];
"pari māgne" two; "astabhnād dyām" four; "namo mitrasya" one; and "yā te dhāmāni" one—thus in the fourth [section] there are twenty-one or twenty, sixty-five or sixty-six *yajus* formulas.

In the fifth chapter: "bhavata naḥ" (two verses), "aṃśuraṃśuḥ" (the *prakṛti* with four pauses), "yujyate" (three verses), "viṣṇornu kam" (three verses), the first two ending in a *yajus*, the *yajus* "viṣṇave tvā", "pari tvā" (one verse), "tvaṃ soma" (five verses), the first being a *gāyatrī* without pause, "juṣāṇaḥ" (a one-word *ekapadā*), the *virāj* ending in a *yajus*, and "uru viṣṇo" (this verse repeated twice)—thus there are seventeen verses in the fifth chapter and one hundred and fifty *yajus* formulas.

In the sixth chapter: "yā te dhāmāni" is one verse; "viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi" are two verses; "idam āpo mahāpaṅktiḥ" is one verse ending with a pause; "deva tvaṣṭar" is one verse; "yad āhur agnyāḥ" is one verse ending with a pause; "haviṣmatīḥ" is one verse; "amūr yāḥ" is one verse; "ahrade tvā śṛṇotv agniḥ" are four verses; "pra te soma" are two verses; "prāg apāk" are two verses. Thus, there are seventeen ṛcs in the sixth chapter, eighty yajus formulas, and in the seventh chapter: "vācaspataye" is one verse; "antaḥ te" is one verse; "vāyav" consists of six verses ending with a yajus. That [section] ends with a yajus.

"yam" (one verse), "venas" (one Yajus at the end), "ye devāsaḥ" (one verse), "mūrdhānam" (one verse), "dhruvam dhruveṇa" (two verses), "ko 'si" (one verse), "indrāgnī āgatam" (ten verses ending in Yajus), "ud u tyam" (four verses)—these are seven Ṛks; thirty-one Yajus, each increasing by eleven syllables;
in the eighth chapter, "kadā cana" (three verses ending in Yajus), "ādityebhyas tvā" (a Yajus), and "śradasmai" (one verse).

"Dve ahaṃ parastāt" is one; "sam indra" is one; "uṃ hi" is one; "agner anīkam" is three; "ejatu" is two; the first two [of those] have three pauses; "mahāpaṅkti"; "maruto yasya" is two; "ātiṣṭha" is three ending with a *yajus*; "yasmān na" is two, the second of which ends with a *yajus*; "saha prāṇena" is a *yajus*; "agne pavasva" is four ending with *yajus*; "ā jighra" is two; "vīna indra" and "vācaspatim" are two; these three also end with *yajus*; "upasṛjan" is two; "yuvantam" has three pauses; "aty aṣṭi"; "yayor ojaḥ" is one; [this is] thirty-four, and that is the *tanva*.

Thus, there are three [verses] in the eighth [chapter]; forty-three *yajus* formulas; and thirty-four [verses] in the ninth chapter. In the ninth chapter: "O God Savitṛ" (*deva savitar*) is one verse; "Of the waters" (*apām rasam*) is a *yajus* at the end; "After the strength" (*vājasyānv*) is one verse; "Within the waters" (*apsvantaravasānā*) is a *purauṣṇih*; "The wind blows" (*vāto vāti*) is three verses; "He desires" (*eṣasya*) is six verses; "Of the strength" (*vājasyeyam*) is seven verses; and "O Agni, be victorious" (*agne sahasva*) is one verse. Thus, in the ninth chapter, there are twenty-two *ṛc*s and eighty-four *yajus* formulas. In the tenth chapter: "O Waters, O Gods" (*apo devāḥ*) is one verse; "At the joint revelry" (*sadhamāde*) is one verse; "Of golden form" (*hiraṇyarūpau*) is one verse ending in a *yajus*; and "You are Mitra, you are Varuṇa" (*mitro 'si varuṇo 'si*) is a *yajus*.

"Of the mountain," one verse; "O Prajāpati," the Evayāmarut formula; "This [is] the Yajus of so-and-so," one verse; "From Indra for me," one verse; "The swan," one verse; "He has sat down," one verse; and "Vāyu is purified," four verses—these are the twelve verses and twelve Yajus formulas in the tenth [Anuvāka], totaling two hundred and twenty.

In the eleventh chapter: the eight verses beginning with *yuñjānaḥ* [are in the Gāyatrī meter]; *stomam* [is] without pause (*anavasānā*); *hastādhāya* [is] one verse ending in a Yajus; *enā* [is] a Yajus in the Anuṣṭubh meter; *pratūrtam* [consists of] four verses, the last of which contains a Yajus; *bhūr antarikṣam* [is] a Yajus; *anv agniḥ* [consists of] eleven verses; *apām pṛṣṭham* [consists of] three verses; *tvām agne* [consists of] six verses; *apo devīḥ* [consists of] ten verses, the ninth of which has three pauses and the last is a single word (*ekapadā*); *oṣadhayaḥ* [consists of] three verses; *āpo hiṣṭhā* [consists of] three verses; *mitraḥ* [consists of] five verses; *kṛttvāya* [is] one verse; *mitttrasya* [consists of] three verses.
In the eleventh chapter, from the beginning up to the end of the *Viśvadeva* hymn, there are seventeen *ṛks* and seventy-six *yajus* formulas.

In the twelfth chapter, because of the abundance of *ṛks*, the *yajus* formulas are counted as [separate] milch-cows; the remaining *ṛks* are four, beginning with "Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu" (*viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si*), while the verse "The swan dwelling in purity" (*haṃsaḥ śuciṣat*) is a *yajus* by virtue of its opening words, ending with "Be thou our wise patron" (*sa bodhi sūriḥ*).

"Viśvakarmaṇe svāhā"—this is a *yajus*; "sañjñānam asi," "agner bhasmāsi," "cit stha," "cidasīti dve," and "sajūr abdaḥ. The remaining one hundred and fourteen *ṛc*s are therein: "suparṇo 'si" with four pauses; "kṛtir namo bhūtyai" is a *virāj* consisting of a single foot; twelve *yajus* and twelve *ṛc*s—thus there are one hundred and fourteen [verses].

In the thirteenth chapter, there are four verses beginning with *mayi gṛhṇāmi*; one verse beginning with *apāṭhāsīt*; eleven verses beginning with *madhu vātā*; nine verses beginning with *samyak sravantī*; six verses beginning with *mā hiṃsīḥ*; at the end of each of the first five [sections], there are two *yajus* formulas; at the end of the chapter, three verses beginning with *lokam tā indram*; and thirteen verses beginning with *lokampṛṇa*, *tā asya indram*, and *viśvā*. Thus, there are fifty-two *ṛc*s and eighty-seven *yajus* formulas.

In the fourteenth chapter, beginning with "dhruvakṣatiḥ," there are five [verses]; four end with the *yajus* formula; at the end of the section beginning with "mūrdhā vayaḥ," there are three ending with *lokantāḥ*; "indram" is one; "indrāgnī" is one; and between these two, "mūrdhāsī" consists of two. When these fourteen *yajus* formulas are collected together according to their metrical structure (*chandobandha*), they amount to [the following]: excluding the three verses ending with *lokantāḥ* and *indram* from the fourteenth [chapter], there are eight *ṛc*s; together with the seventeen *yajus* formulas, this totals one hundred and fifty-four.

In the fifteenth chapter, there are two verses beginning with *agnerjātān*, one beginning with *agneḥ purīṣam*, and one beginning with *agnirmūrdhā*—making thirty-one. Among these, *agniṃ hotāram* has three pauses; *agne tvaṃ naḥ* consists of three two-footed verses; *yena ṛṣayaḥ* comprises eight [verses]; and *lokampṛṇā* consists of four [verses]. Thus, in the fifteenth chapter, there are fifteen ṛcas and forty-six yajus formulas, totaling ninety-five. In the sixteenth chapter, there are sixteen [verses] beginning with *namaste*; seventeen beginning with *drāpe 'ndhasaspate*. Thus, in the sixteenth chapter, there are thirty-three ṛcas and one hundred and thirty-two [yajus formulas].
In the seventeenth chapter, there are four [verses] beginning with *aśmannūrjam*; one beginning with *imāmagnaḥ*; five beginning with *nṛṣade veṭ*; and one addressed to Indra.
"Daivīḥ"—this one [verse] is extracted; thus the *yajus* formulas are eleven, and the *ṛc*s are ninety-five.

In the eighteenth chapter, "Vājasya nu" consists of seven [verses]; "Sa no bhuvanasya" is one; "Yāste" consists of four; and from "Agniṃ yunajmi" until the end of the chapter are the *ṛc*s. Having extracted the name, there is one *yajus*, and another [set of] twenty-seven. In the eighteenth [chapter], there are thirty-six *ṛc*s and sixty-eight *yajus* formulas, totaling three hundred and sixty-eight.

In the nineteenth chapter, there are eighty-four verses from "svādūkṣvā" down to the end of the chapter, excluding the four verses beginning with "pitṛbhyaḥ," the three-avasa Mahāpaṅkti verse beginning with "tavedaṃ haviḥ," and the two three-avasa verses beginning with "reto mūtram. Thus, in the nineteenth [chapter], there are ninety-four Ṛg-verses and thirty Yajus-formulas.

In the twentieth chapter: the source of the Kṣatra is the *dvipadā gāyatrī* "niṣasāda" (one verse); "ko 'si" (six verses) with the last [verse] having three pauses; "trayo devāḥ" is a *pañkti* with three pauses; "lomāni" is one verse; "yad devāḥ" consists of three verses; "samudre te" is a *dvipadā virāj*; "drupadād iva" consists of three verses; "samāvavarti" is one verse; "abhyādadhāni" is the final [section] of the chapter consisting of six [verses]; and "vṛṣṭibhya upayāma" is a Yajus formula. In the twentieth [chapter], there are eighty-four Ṛks and fourteen Yajus formulas.

In the twenty-first chapter, there are twenty verses beginning with "imamme varuṇa" (1.24.14); the remaining formulas from "hotā yakṣat" until the end of the chapter are *yajus* mantras, consisting of thirty-three verses and twenty-eight *yajus* formulas. In the twenty-second chapter, there is one verse beginning with "imāmagṛbhṇan" (1.35.1), one beginning with "yo arvantaṃ" (1.35.6), ten beginning with "tat savitur" (4.53.1–10), and one beginning with "viśvo devasya" (5.50.1)—thus thirteen verses in the twenty-second; and one hundred and thirteen *yajus* formulas.

In the twenty-third chapter, from "hiraṇyagarbha" to "utsakthyāvaguda," there are forty-five verses (ṛcas) and fifty-eight sacrificial formulas (yajūṃṣi). In the twenty-fourth chapter, beginning with "aśvastūpara" until the end of the chapter, all are sacrificial formulas. In the twenty-fifth chapter, from "śādandadbhiḥ" up to "tvaca," all are sacrificial formulas; "jumbakāya" is a two-footed verse (dvipadā); and from "hiraṇyagarbha" up to "haviṣmān," there are thirty-six verses. Now, "imā nu... [follows].
The hymn beginning with *kam* consists of six verses; there are twenty-five hymns [in total] comprising forty-three verses.

In the twenty-sixth chapter, the hymn beginning with *priyo devānām* has one verse and lacks a final pause (*avasāna*). The twenty-four hymns ending the chapter beginning with *bṛhaspate* consist of twenty-five verses in the twenty-sixth chapter. There are seven sacrificial formulas (*yajus*), eight of which end with a *yajus*. In the twenty-seventh chapter, the hymn beginning with *samāstvāgne* has ten verses; *uddhāsya* has twelve; *pīvo'nnāni* has twelve; *abhitvā* has ten; and the sacrificial formula beginning with *saṃvatsaro'si* is one. Thus, in the twenty-seventh chapter, there are forty-four verses and one sacrificial formula.
In the twenty-eighth chapter, there are the *yajus* formulas beginning with "hotā yakṣat" and so forth; thus, all these *yajus* number forty-six.

In the twenty-ninth chapter, there are fifty-seven verses beginning with "samiddho añjan," dedicated to Agni; and starting from "kṛṣṇo agnīva" until the end of the chapter, there are thirty-two *yajus* formulas.
In the thirtieth chapter, there are three verses beginning with "deva savitar," and all the subsequent formulas until the end of the chapter total one hundred and seventy-seven *yajus*.
In the thirty-first chapter, there are twenty-two verses beginning with *sahasraśīrṣā*.

In the thirty-second chapter, there are sixteen verses beginning with *tadevāgniḥ*. Among those, the third verse, *na tasya pratimā asti*, is a two-footed *gāyatrī*. The following are mentioned by their initial words (*pratīka*): *hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*, *yaḥ prāṇataḥ*, *yasyeme*, and *kadā cana*—these four; *mā mā hiṃsīḥ*—this one; *ayasmayaṃ na*—these two; and *āpo ha yad*—these two. These are the verses cited by their opening phrases.

Together with those twenty-five verses, all the verses from the beginning of this chapter up to the end of the chapter "asyā jarāyu" (3.33) amount to twenty-two, as indicated by their initial words (*pratīka*). Together with those one hundred and nineteen verses,
the fifty-eight verses from "yaj jāgrataḥ" (3.34) up to the end of that chapter are likewise included.

Thus, including the four [verses] mentioned by their pratīkas, there are sixty-two verses in the thirty-fifth chapter; [furthermore], "apeto yantu" and so forth consist of twenty-one verses; "dyubhir ahobhiḥ" is one *yajus*; "vāyuḥ punātu" consists of four *yajus* formulas; "apa naḥ" is one verse; and there are twenty-one verses and six *yajus* formulas.

In the thirty-sixth chapter: *yan ma* is one verse; *tat savituḥ* consists of six verses; *indro viśvasya virāṭ* is a two-footed verse; *śanno mitra* consists of nine verses; *ahāniśam* is a two-footed Gāyatrī; *namaste* consists of three verses; *taccakṣuḥ* is one verse with a Yajus in the middle; there are six verses with a Yajus at the beginning and a Yajus at the end. Thus, in the thirty-sixth [chapter], there are twenty Ṛks and Yajuses. And in the twenty-first chapter: *yuñjate* is one verse; *ā pra it* is one verse; *dhartā divaḥ* consists of two verses; *hṛde tvā* is one verse. In the thirty-seventh [chapter], there are five verses and Yajuses, totaling thirty-one.

In the thirty-eighth chapter: "yaste stana" is one verse; "viśvāśā" is one; "aśvinā gharmam" consists of two; "abhīmam" consists of two; these [last four] are Gāyatrīs and Bṛhatīs with no pause in the middle, or they may be Atiśakvarīs with pauses at every three syllables; "kṣatrasya tvā" consists of four; "ud vayam" is one; "yāvatī" consists of two; "payaso retaḥ" is a Gāyatrī with no pause, and there is one [additional] Ekā; thus in the thirty-eighth [chapter], there are thirteen or fourteen Ṛks and fifty-two Yajus formulas.
In the thirty-ninth chapter, there is one [verse] beginning with *manasaḥ kāmam*, and two Ṛg-verses beginning with *ekaḥ* and *ugraśca bhīmaśca*.

In the fortieth chapter, there are seventeen verses consisting of fourteen beginning with *īśā vāsyam* and two beginning with *agne naya*; two Yajus-formulas beginning with *vāyuranilam*; either the Gāyatrī beginning with *om*, or three Yajus-formulas beginning with *krato*; and four Yajus-formulas beginning with *hiraṇmayena pātreṇa* and *khaṃ brahma*. This is the division of the number of Ṛks and Yajus.
All the *ṛc* verses, unified by the sage who is the ground of the six Vedas, should be known as four hundred and three; and likewise, all the *yajus* formulas, by the wise Vasiṣṭha,
are four hundred and eighty-two.
Alternatively, according to the division in the *Saṃhitā*, it is "five less";
thus ends the Vasiṣṭha *Śikṣā*, which consists of the division of the *Ṛg* and *Yajus*.
